title: Transport Systems in Mammals
seo_title: Grade 10 Life Sciences: Transport Systems in Mammals Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 10 Life Sciences: Transport systems in mammals
standard_text: The circulatory system: the structure and functions of the heart; the cardiac cycle; blood vessels (arteries, veins and capillaries); double circulation (pulmonary and systemic); blood and its components; the lymphatic system; cardiovascular diseases. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 10, Life Sciences: Transport systems in mammals)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the heart, the cardiac cycle, blood vessels, double circulation, blood and cardiovascular diseases. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
body_html:
How to think about it

The heart has four chambers: two atria receive blood and two ventricles pump it out. Valves stop blood from flowing backwards. The right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs (pulmonary circulation); the left side pumps oxygenated blood to the body (systemic circulation).

Arteries have thick, elastic walls to carry blood at high pressure; veins have valves and carry blood back to the heart; capillaries have walls one cell thick for exchange. Blood is made of plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.

Example

Which chamber pumps blood to the body?

It has the thickest wall.

Answer: the left ventricle

Example

Why do veins have valves?

Blood pressure is low.

Answer: to stop blood flowing backwards

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all arteries carry oxygenated blood (the pulmonary artery does not).
  • Thinking the heart's left side is on your right when you look at a diagram.
  • Mixing up atria and ventricles.

faq.q: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker?
faq.a: It must pump blood all round the body, which needs more pressure.

faq.q: How can you reduce the risk of heart disease?
faq.a: Exercise, do not smoke, and eat less salt and saturated fat.

items.q: One cardiac cycle on an ECG lasts 1,2 s. Calculate the heart rate in beats per minute.
items.e: Heart rate = 60 ÷ 1,2 = 50,0 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Cardiac output is 9,00 dm³ min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 60 cm³. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 9 000 ÷ 60 = 150 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Does the vena cava carry oxygenated or deoxygenated blood?
items.e: The vena cava carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the right atrium.

items.q: Cardiac output is 5,20 dm³ min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 65 cm³. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 5 200 ÷ 65 = 80 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Cardiac output is 6,00 dm³ min⁻¹ and heart rate is 75 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in cm³.
items.e: SV = CO ÷ HR = 6 000 cm³ ÷ 75 = 80 cm³.

items.q: Stroke volume is 100 cm³ and heart rate is 150 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in dm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 15 000 cm³ min⁻¹ = 15,0 dm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: Does the aorta carry oxygenated or deoxygenated blood?
items.e: The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body.

items.q: Does the pulmonary artery carry oxygenated or deoxygenated blood?
items.e: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

items.q: One cardiac cycle on an ECG lasts 0,75 s. Calculate the heart rate in beats per minute.
items.e: Heart rate = 60 ÷ 0,75 = 80,0 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: What is the role of platelets?
c: carrying the impulse down the interventricular septum
releasing factors that help blood clot
items.e: Platelets: releasing factors that help blood clot.

items.q: Which blood group is the universal donor?
items.e: Its cells carry no A or B antigen.

items.q: Cardiac output is 6,60 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 110 mL. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 6 600 ÷ 110 = 60 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for becoming macrophages that engulf germs?
items.e: Monocytes: becoming macrophages that engulf germs.

items.q: What is the role of monocytes?
c: releasing factors that help blood clot
items.e: Monocytes: becoming macrophages that engulf germs.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the lungs to the left atrium?
items.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.

items.q: Cardiac output is 10,8 dm³ min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 120 cm³. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 10 800 ÷ 120 = 90 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Cardiac output is 14,4 dm³ min⁻¹ and heart rate is 120 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in cm³.
A person has a tidal volume of 0,40 L and breathes 30 times per minute. Calculate the pulmonary ventilation rate.
items.e: Pulmonary ventilation = tidal volume × breathing rate = 12,0 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs?
items.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.

items.q: Stroke volume is 60 mL and heart rate is 60 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 3 600 mL min⁻¹ = 3,60 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which describes a capillary?
c: It has a thick, muscular, elastic wall to withstand high pressure.
It has no wall at all.
It has a wall only one cell thick.
It has a thinner wall and valves to stop blood flowing backwards.
items.e: A capillary has a wall only one cell thick.

items.q: A person has a heart rate of 90 beats per minute and a stroke volume of 75 cm³. What is the cardiac output in dm³ per minute?
items.e: Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume = 90 × 75 = 6 750 cm³/min.

items.q: Blood is in the pulmonary artery. Where does it go next?
items.e: Body → vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body.

items.q: Blood enters the left atrium. Where has it just come from?
items.e: Follow the double circulation backwards.

items.q: Does the coronary artery carry oxygenated or deoxygenated blood?
items.e: The coronary artery carries oxygenated blood to the muscle of the heart wall.

items.q: Blood is in the aorta. Where does it go next?
items.e: Body → vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body.

items.q: A learner counts 22 pulse beats in 20 seconds. What is the heart rate in beats per minute?
items.e: Heart rate = 22 × (60 ÷ 20).

items.q: Which describes an artery?
c: It has a thinner wall and valves to stop blood flowing backwards.
It has a wall only one cell thick.
It has a thick, muscular, elastic wall to withstand high pressure.
It has no wall at all.
items.e: An artery has a thick, muscular, elastic wall to withstand high pressure.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
items.e: An artery carries blood away from the heart.

items.q: Blood enters the right ventricle. Where has it just come from?
items.e: Follow the double circulation backwards.

items.q: Blood enters the pulmonary vein. Where has it just come from?
items.e: Follow the double circulation backwards.

items.q: Which blood vessel has a thick, muscular, elastic wall to withstand high pressure?
items.e: An artery has a thick, muscular, elastic wall to withstand high pressure.

items.q: Blood enters the pulmonary artery. Where has it just come from?
items.e: Follow the double circulation backwards.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the small intestine to the liver?
items.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the aorta to the kidney?
items.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood back to the heart?
items.e: A vein carries blood back to the heart.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the body to the right atrium?
items.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.

items.q: Which blood vessel has a wall only one cell thick?
items.e: A capillary has a wall only one cell thick.

items.q: Blood is in the left atrium. Where does it go next?
items.e: Body → vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body.

items.q: Blood is in the right atrium. Where does it go next?
items.e: Body → vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body.

items.q: Which is the hepatic portal system?
c: veins that carry blood from the intestine to the liver before it returns to the heart
items.e: The liver processes absorbed food.

items.q: What is atherosclerosis (coronary artery disease)?
c: narrowing of the arteries by deposits of calcium, fat and cholesterol
items.e: It can lead to a heart attack.

items.q: What is angina pectoris?
c: acute chest pain when not enough oxygen reaches the heart muscle
items.e: It is a warning sign of heart disease.

items.q: What is the role of basophils?
c: the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat
the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic
items.e: Basophils: secreting histamine, serotonin and heparin.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for forming fibrin threads in clotting?
items.e: Fibrinogen: forming fibrin threads in clotting.

items.q: What is the role of lymphocytes?
c: B and T cells of the immune response
carrying the impulse down the interventricular septum
items.e: Lymphocytes: B and T cells of the immune response.

items.q: What is the life span of a red blood cell?
items.e: They are destroyed in the spleen.

items.q: Which sound of the heart is 'lub'?
c: the closing of the semilunar valves
the closing of the tricuspid and bicuspid (AV) valves
items.e: 'Dub' is the closing of the semilunar valves.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat?
items.e: SA node: the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic?
items.e: Neutrophils: the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic.

items.q: What is the role of bundle of His?
c: the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat
carrying the impulse down the interventricular septum
items.e: Bundle of His: carrying the impulse down the interventricular septum.

items.q: What is the role of SA node?
c: the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat
items.e: SA node: the pacemaker that starts each heartbeat.

items.q: How many heartbeats does a healthy adult have each minute at rest?
items.e: It is set by the SA node.

items.q: Which condition can occur when an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive baby for the second time?
items.e: Her anti-Rh antibodies destroy the baby's red cells.

items.q: What is the stroke volume of a healthy adult heart?
items.e: Cardiac output = 72 × 70 mL ≈ 5 L per minute.

items.q: What is the normal blood pressure of a healthy adult?
items.e: Systolic over diastolic.

items.q: How many litres of blood does a healthy adult have?
items.e: Plasma is about 55% of it.

items.q: Which type of circulation do fishes have?
items.e: Blood passes through the heart once per circuit.

items.q: What is the role of fibrinogen?
c: B and T cells of the immune response
carrying the impulse down the interventricular septum
items.e: Fibrinogen: forming fibrin threads in clotting.

items.q: What is the role of AV node?
c: passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles
releasing factors that help blood clot
B and T cells of the immune response
items.e: AV node: passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles?
items.e: AV node: passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles.

items.q: Pulmonary ventilation is 40,0 L min⁻¹ at 20 breaths per minute. Calculate the tidal volume.
items.e: Tidal volume = ventilation ÷ breathing rate = 2,00 L.

items.q: Cardiac output is 7,50 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 100 mL. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 7 500 ÷ 100 = 75 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Cardiac output is 9,00 L min⁻¹ and heart rate is 150 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in mL.
Pulmonary ventilation is 30,0 L min⁻¹ at 20 breaths per minute. Calculate the tidal volume.
items.e: Tidal volume = ventilation ÷ breathing rate = 1,50 L.

items.q: Cardiac output is 4,68 L min⁻¹ and heart rate is 72 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in mL.
What is double circulation?
c: blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit: pulmonary and systemic
items.e: Found in birds and mammals.

items.q: Stroke volume is 120 mL and heart rate is 120 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 14 400 mL min⁻¹ = 14,4 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Cardiac output is 9,60 L min⁻¹ and heart rate is 80 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in mL.
Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for releasing factors that help blood clot?
items.e: Platelets: releasing factors that help blood clot.

items.q: One cardiac cycle on an ECG lasts 0,40 s. Calculate the heart rate in beats per minute.
items.e: Heart rate = 60 ÷ 0,40 = 150 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Cardiac output is 5,25 L min⁻¹ and heart rate is 70 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in mL.
Cardiac output is 13,5 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 75 mL. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 13 500 ÷ 75 = 180 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Cardiac output is 7,20 L min⁻¹ and heart rate is 72 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in mL.
Stroke volume is 120 mL and heart rate is 90 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 10 800 mL min⁻¹ = 10,8 L min⁻¹.

items.q: What is the role of eosinophils?
c: the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic
items.e: Eosinophils: resisting infections and allergic reactions.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for carrying the impulse down the interventricular septum?
items.e: Bundle of His: carrying the impulse down the interventricular septum.

items.q: Cardiac output is 10,8 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 90 mL. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 10 800 ÷ 90 = 120 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Stroke volume is 75 mL and heart rate is 70 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 5 250 mL min⁻¹ = 5,25 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Cardiac output is 7,00 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 70 mL. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 7 000 ÷ 70 = 100 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Which blood group has antigen B on its red blood cells?
items.e: Blood group B: antigen B on the red cells, anti-A in the plasma.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for resisting infections and allergic reactions?
items.e: Eosinophils: resisting infections and allergic reactions.

items.q: Which blood group has anti-B in its plasma?
items.e: Blood group A has anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: Why does a diet high in saturated fat and cholesterol increase the risk of coronary heart disease?
c: Nicotine and carbon monoxide damage artery walls and raise blood pressure.
It is linked to high blood pressure and obesity.
Fatty deposits build up in the coronary arteries.
items.e: In coronary heart disease, the coronary arteries are narrowed by fatty deposits (atherosclerosis), so less oxygen reaches the heart muscle.

items.q: Why does lack of exercise increase the risk of coronary heart disease?
c: It is linked to high blood pressure and obesity.
Fatty deposits build up in the coronary arteries.
items.e: In coronary heart disease, the coronary arteries are narrowed by fatty deposits (atherosclerosis), so less oxygen reaches the heart muscle.

items.q: Which antibodies are in the plasma of blood group AB?
items.e: Blood group AB has no antibodies in the plasma.

items.q: Why does stress increase the risk of coronary heart disease?
c: It is linked to high blood pressure and obesity.
Nicotine and carbon monoxide damage artery walls and raise blood pressure.
items.e: In coronary heart disease, the coronary arteries are narrowed by fatty deposits (atherosclerosis), so less oxygen reaches the heart muscle.

items.q: Stroke volume is 70 mL and heart rate is 180 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 12 600 mL min⁻¹ = 12,6 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which antibodies are in the plasma of blood group O?
items.e: Blood group O has anti-A and anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: Stroke volume is 80 mL and heart rate is 150 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 12 000 mL min⁻¹ = 12,0 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which substance in cigarette smoke: it is addictive and raises heart rate and blood pressure.
items.e: Nicotine addicts; tar causes cancer; carbon monoxide reduces oxygen carried.

items.q: Cardiac output is 6,40 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 100 mL. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 6 400 ÷ 100 = 64 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for B and T cells of the immune response?
items.e: Lymphocytes: B and T cells of the immune response.

items.q: Why does smoking increase the risk of coronary heart disease?
c: Fatty deposits build up in the coronary arteries.
Nicotine and carbon monoxide damage artery walls and raise blood pressure.
items.e: In coronary heart disease, the coronary arteries are narrowed by fatty deposits (atherosclerosis), so less oxygen reaches the heart muscle.

items.q: Which substance in cigarette smoke: it joins with red blood cells and reduces how much oxygen the blood can carry.
items.e: Nicotine addicts; tar causes cancer; carbon monoxide reduces oxygen carried.

items.q: What is lymph?
c: tissue fluid in lymph vessels, containing lymphocytes
items.e: It returns fluid to the blood.

items.q: Which antibodies are in the plasma of blood group A?
items.e: Blood group A has anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: Which antigen is on the red blood cells of a person with blood group AB?
items.e: Blood group AB: antigens A and B on the red cells, no antibodies in the plasma.

items.q: Which blood group has anti-A and anti-B in its plasma?
items.e: Blood group O has anti-A and anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: What harm does particles of soot in cigarette smoke do?
c: It coats the lungs and causes cancer.
They irritate the airways and damage the alveoli.
It is addictive and raises heart rate and blood pressure.
It joins with red blood cells and reduces how much oxygen the blood can carry.
items.e: Tobacco smoke contains thousands of chemicals.
